item: 9.10 — the Thinking switch is locked on for a model whose roster row says supportsThinkingOff:false (2026-11-22)
branch: syncModelFooter reads the selected roster row's supportsThinkingOff: false = switch disabled and drawn on, with its own title; true, an absent key or no roster row = the switch works as before and shows the thinking preference
provenance: The first three roster rows are copied VERBATIM from the CLI's bare initialize response on 2.1.330 (2026-11-22 audit); the fourth (haiku, no supportsThinkingOff key) is the 2.1.241 row from fixture 55 and stands for an older CLI that sends no such key. That the flag tracks behaviour was probed live over stdio with the panel's flags on 2.1.330, 2026-11-22, a control turn and a set_max_thinking_tokens 0 turn per model on the same prompt: flag true — Haiku 4.5 (1 thinking block -> 0) and Sonnet 5 (1 -> 0); flag false — Haiku 5.5 (1 -> 1) and Sonnet 5.5 (1 -> 1), the 0 acked with success every time. The __models and __thinking frames are OUR OWN Kotlin->webview frames (self-consistency only). The roster is switched by injected __models frames, never setModel, and the switch is never clicked while enabled, so nothing is persisted and nothing reaches the live CLI; the click on the locked switch goes through tglThink.onclick directly with window.__bridge wrapped, because a browser fires no click on a disabled button and the handler's own guard is what is under test. The last step puts back the saved roster, selection and thinking preference. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-11-22 against the pre-change webview (whole webview/ dir stashed back to 0efe93b, sandbox restarted, control verified BY CONTENT: syncModelFooter has no supportsThinkingOff): 9 passed / 9 failed — all seven DISCRIMINATING asserts failed (not disabled, drawn off, aria false, old title, not locked with the preference on, 1 bridge frame sent, preference flipped) plus step 2's two guards that depend on the lock; every other guard passed.

steps.note: flag false: the switch is locked and drawn on, even with the thinking preference off; flag true and an absent key: it works and shows the preference
